summary: Senmyo Naniwa works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University under Mohan G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, Purushottam Vishvanath Bapat, and Genjun Sasaki. He held posts at Bukkyo University and Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Sensho Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University from around 1962 to 1971 and later served as a professor there from circa 1988 to 2009.

Sensho Murakami was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani and Toyo universities. He served as a lecturer and professor at the University of Tokyo (1888, 1917–1923) and also taught at Komazawa, Toyo, and Otani universities.

Seok-hyeong Kim was a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He served as a professor at Dongguk University from circa 1953 to 1969 and as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. As of 2026, he is the Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University.

Seongjoon Cheong is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his Ph.D. at Dongguk University (1995–1999). He served as a research fellow at the Translation Institute of Tibetan Buddhist Canon and a research professor at Uiduk University.

Seraphim Rose worked in religious studies and philosophy, studying under Alan Watts and at the California Institute of Integral Studies, UC Berkeley, and USC. He was affiliated with the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the United States.

Sergej Konstantinovich Bulich was a linguist and Indologist who earned his M.A. at Kazan State University before studying at Berlin, Jena, and Leipzig. He was a docent at Kazan (1885) and became extraordinary professor at Saint Petersburg State University (1891).

Sergey Burmistrov is a philosopher and Indologist who earned his D.Sci. at Saint Petersburg State University. He served as assistant professor there, associate professor at Saint Petersburg State University of Culture and Arts, and leading researcher at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Sergey Malov was a scholar of Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kazan Theological Academy and Saint Petersburg State University. He directed several Kazan institutes and headed the Turkic Languages Sector at the Institute of Linguistics.

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Central Asian scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University, where he later became a professor. He served as perpetual secretary of the Russian Academy of Sciences and directed the Asiatic Museum and Institute of Oriental Studies.

Sergiu Anatol Al-George was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied under Mircea Eliade, earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and University of Delhi, and held a post at the University of Bucharest from 1971 to 1973.

Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies who completed her Ph.D. at Columbia University under Alex Wayman. She held posts at Southern Methodist University and the American Museum of Natural History.
Sesso Oda was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under and succeeded traditional teacher Zuigan Goto. He taught students including Gary Snyder and Soko Morinaga.

Seth Segall, working in Buddhist studies and philosophy, received his PhD from Southern Illinois University Carbondale. He served as an assistant clinical professor at Yale School of Medicine (1981–2017) and lecturer at Purchase College, SUNY (2012–2017).
Seton Uhlhorn is an Indology scholar who studied at Harvard University, where he has been a Ph.D. candidate in South Asian studies and served as an instructional fellow in Hindi-Urdu.

Seung-yeon Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who completed doctoral studies under Lee Sang-hae. Lee has held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Seoul National University and a PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh held posts at Geumgang University and became an associate professor at Seoul National University in 2025.
Seungsahn Haengwon was a Buddhist figure who studied at Dongguk University and under Kobong Sunim, whom he succeeded in 1957. He founded the Kwan Um School of Zen in 1970.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester. He served as a lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds (attested 2005).
